evals.expected_output: Runs the full autonomous pipeline: loads config (or creates defaults silently), reads CLAUDE.md constitution, snapshots the board via gh project CLI, defaults to board-hygiene goal, generates changeset, auto-applies operations with confidence >= 0.70, prints machine-parseable summary. No AskUserQuestion prompts at any point.
expectations: The skill detects autonomous mode from the --autonomous flag and does NOT call AskUserQuestion at any point during the entire run
The skill reads .claude/CLAUDE.md (or CLAUDE.md) and extracts constitution dimensions — reporting a completeness score like 'N/6 dimensions'
The skill runs 'gh project list --owner @me --format json' or uses config to determine the board, then runs 'gh project field-list' and 'gh project item-list' to snapshot board state
The skill defaults to 'board-hygiene' goal when no goal text is provided after the flag
The changeset includes operations with confidence scores (0.0-1.0) and only auto-applies operations at or above the 0.70 threshold
The skill runs 'gh project item-archive', 'gh project item-add', or 'gh project item-edit' commands for the auto-applied operations
The summary output includes: repo name, board reference, goal, constitution completeness, applied count, suggestions count, and board state after changes

evals.prompt: I want to plan my next sprint. I have a bunch of issues piling up and need to decide what goes into the next 2-week sprint.
evals.expected_output: The skill enters interactive mode, elicits the session goal via AskUserQuestion (user should pick sprint planning), reads constitution and board, generates a changeset that includes hygiene ops plus scored item selection for the sprint, presents the changeset for approval before executing.
expectations: The skill presents a goal elicitation question via AskUserQuestion with options including 'Board hygiene', 'Sprint planning', 'Prioritize', 'Board sync', and 'Custom goal'
The skill reads the CLAUDE.md constitution and extracts available dimensions for alignment scoring
The skill snapshots the board and also fetches open issues ('gh issue list --state open') and PRs ('gh pr list --state open') for the current repo
The changeset includes board-hygiene operations first (archive stale Done items, flag stale In Progress) PLUS sprint-specific operations that score and select unplanned items for the sprint
Sprint item selection references signals: label priority, milestone proximity, dependency count, and constitution alignment (if constitution completeness >= 70%)
The full changeset is presented to the user for approval before any mutations are executed — interactive mode never auto-applies without confirmation
The summary shows board state before and after, including how many items were added to the sprint

evals.prompt: /project-plan --dry-run --autonomous clean up the board and sync orphaned issues
evals.expected_output: Runs autonomous pipeline with board-sync + board-hygiene goals inferred from the text, generates the full changeset, prints it as a formatted table showing each operation with confidence scores, but does NOT execute any mutations. No gh project item-edit/archive/add commands should run.
expectations: The skill parses both --dry-run and --autonomous flags from $ARGUMENTS

The skill detects the goal from the remaining argument text — 'clean up' maps to board-hygiene and 'sync orphaned issues' maps to board-sync, resulting in combined board-hygiene + board-sync operations
The changeset output is a formatted table showing operation type (ARCHIVE, ADD, MOVE, EDIT), target item description, field, from/to values, confidence score, and reason for each operation
The changeset distinguishes auto-apply operations (confidence >= 0.70, marked with checkmark) from suggestions (below threshold, marked with flag)
The skill does NOT execute any mutations — no 'gh project item-archive', 'gh project item-add', or 'gh project item-edit' commands are run
The output includes a count summary line like 'CHANGESET (N operations, M auto-apply, K suggestions)'

evals.prompt:
/project-plan --autonomous

Here is the repo's CLAUDE.md:

# My Library
A utility library for string manipulation.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads this sparse 2-line CLAUDE.md, scores constitution completeness below 50% (only 1/6 dimensions found — Mission/Purpose), skips alignment scoring entirely, and still proceeds with board-hygiene operations. Does not fail, warn loudly, or ask for more constitution detail.
expectations: The skill extracts whatever it can from the sparse CLAUDE.md — at minimum the Mission/Purpose dimension ('utility library for string manipulation')
The constitution completeness score is below 50% (at most 1-2 of 6 dimensions found: Mission, Branching, Build & Test, Commit Conventions, Active Priorities, Constraints)
The skill explicitly notes that alignment scoring is skipped due to insufficient constitution completeness — it does not attempt to score changeset operations against constitution principles
The skill still proceeds with board-hygiene operations normally — sparse CLAUDE.md does not block or degrade board operations
The skill does NOT prompt the user to improve their CLAUDE.md or warn that constitution is 'incomplete' — it treats sparse input as expected reality across the 190-repo fleet

evals.expected_output: Prints a man-page formatted help output with PROJECT-PLAN(1) GPM Skills Manual header, covering NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, MODES, FLAGS, EXAMPLES sections. Does not execute any phases or read any files.
expectations: The output follows man-page format with 'PROJECT-PLAN(1)' and 'GPM Skills Manual' in the header
The output includes a NAME section describing what the skill does
The output includes a SYNOPSIS section showing the command format with flags: --autonomous, --ui-ops, --dry-run, and optional goal text
The output includes a DESCRIPTION or MODES section explaining autonomous, interactive, and dry-run modes
The output includes at least 2 usage EXAMPLES showing real invocations (e.g., '/project-plan --autonomous', '/project-plan plan my sprint')
The skill does NOT read CLAUDE.md, snapshot the board, or execute any planning phases — help output is the complete response

evals.prompt:
/project-plan --autonomous

Note: This repository has no GitHub Projects v2 board configured. gh project list returns an empty result.
evals.expected_output: When no GitHub Projects v2 board exists for the user/org, the skill handles this gracefully in autonomous mode: detects the absence via 'gh project list', skips all board operations without error, and prints a summary noting that no board was found. Does not offer to create a board (that's interactive-only behavior).
expectations: The skill runs 'gh project list --owner @me --format json' (or equivalent) and detects that no boards exist or no boards match the config
In autonomous mode, the skill does NOT call AskUserQuestion to offer board creation — it skips board operations silently
The skill prints a summary that clearly indicates no board was found and board operations were skipped
The skill does NOT crash, throw an error, or exit with a non-zero status — it degrades gracefully
The skill still reads the CLAUDE.md constitution (board absence doesn't skip constitution reading)
If running in interactive mode instead, the skill WOULD offer to create a board via AskUserQuestion — this is the behavioral difference between modes

evals.prompt:
/project-plan --autonomous --ui-ops

Assume Chrome DevTools MCP tools are available (navigate_page, take_screenshot, click, drag, wait_for).
evals.expected_output: After completing the standard Phase 0-5 pipeline, the skill enters Phase 6 (UI Operations) because --ui-ops was specified. It navigates to the GitHub Projects board in Chrome, takes a verification screenshot, performs UI-only operations (view creation, item reordering), and verifies each operation with a follow-up screenshot.
expectations: The skill runs the full Phase 0-5 pipeline (config, constitution, board snapshot, goal, changeset, execution) before entering Phase 6
Phase 6 uses Chrome DevTools MCP tools: navigate_page to open the board URL (github.com/users/{owner}/projects/{number}), take_screenshot to verify state
The skill performs at least one UI-specific operation that has no CLI equivalent — such as creating a board view, reordering items within a column, or configuring board-level settings
Each UI operation is followed by a verification screenshot (take_screenshot) to confirm the change took effect

evals.prompt:
/project-plan --autonomous --ui-ops

Note: Chrome DevTools MCP tools are NOT available in this session. ToolSearch for chrome-devtools returns no results.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that Chrome DevTools MCP tools are unavailable despite --ui-ops being requested. It completes Phases 0-5 normally via CLI/API, then skips Phase 6 entirely with an informational note. No crash, no error.
expectations: The skill checks for Chrome DevTools MCP tool availability before entering Phase 6
The skill detects that Chrome DevTools tools are NOT available (ToolSearch returns no matches)
Phase 6 is skipped entirely — no navigate_page, take_screenshot, click, or drag calls are attempted
The skill prints an informational note explaining that UI operations were skipped because Chrome DevTools MCP is not available
The skill does NOT crash, throw an error, or abort — Phases 0-5 complete normally and the summary is still printed
The summary includes the note about skipped UI operations so the user knows to enable Chrome DevTools for next time

evals.prompt:
/project-plan --autonomous --ui-ops

Assume Chrome DevTools MCP tools are available. During view creation, the first take_screenshot verification shows the view was NOT created (element not found in snapshot). Simulate a UI operation failure.
evals.expected_output: The skill attempts a UI operation, detects the verification failure via take_screenshot, retries the operation once, and if verification still fails, skips that operation with a warning and continues to the next UI operation.
expectations: The skill attempts a UI operation (e.g., view creation) using click/fill via Chrome DevTools MCP
After the operation, take_screenshot or take_snapshot is used to verify the result
The verification detects that the operation did not succeed (expected element not found)
The skill retries the operation exactly once — not zero times, not more than once
After the retry fails verification again, the skill skips that operation with a warning message
The skill continues to the next UI operation rather than aborting Phase 6 entirely

evals.prompt:
Let's review the project board together and figure out priorities.

During the session, after the changeset is presented, the user responds: "looks good, just do it"
evals.expected_output: The skill starts in interactive mode, elicits goals, generates changeset, presents it for approval. When the user says 'just do it', the skill detects this as a conversational mode shift to autonomous and applies the changeset without further confirmation prompts.
expectations: The skill starts in interactive mode (no --autonomous flag) and presents a goal elicitation question via AskUserQuestion
After goal selection and changeset generation, the changeset is presented to the user for approval
When the user responds with 'just do it', the skill detects this phrase as a conversational mode shift signal
The skill switches to autonomous_mode = true for the remaining execution phases
The skill applies all changeset operations with confidence >= 0.70 without further AskUserQuestion prompts
The summary confirms that autonomous mode was activated mid-session via conversational shift
